video.title: The Most Valuable Skill in Business

summary: Marcus explains how he uses Google Ads and YouTube Ads to help local service businesses generate leads, and Chris Koerner asks which niches and offers work best. Marcus describes researching competitors, improving landing pages, targeting YouTube audiences, remarketing, and letting campaigns mature. The examples include cleaning, roofing, solar, and a hypnosis practice, with results that vary by market and by the client’s ability to close leads. His advice for a new marketer is to get testimonials through free work, make the landing page clear, and be patient.

He gives performance figures from student and client campaigns, but does not state his own agency margins or fees.

acquisition.how: His described agency acquisition relies on personal outreach and network relationships; automated prospecting would need to respect UK marketing rules.

onboarding.how: Forms and account access could be handled with software, but research and agreeing on goals require client input.

delivery.how: Agents could draft copy, analyze campaigns, and suggest tests; strategy, client approvals, and account decisions still need regular human review.

billing.how: Recurring invoicing could be automated, though Marcus does not describe his billing process.

tactics.name: Choose niches with enough customer value
steps: Prioritize recurring or high-ticket local services whose customer lifetime value is in the thousands.
Check local competition because the same niche can perform differently between nearby markets.
Do not assume that a low one-off customer value will support paid acquisition.

quote.text: So, you want to have a a business where your the lifetime value of a client is in the thousands.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Research competitors before taking on a campaign
steps: Check whether the business category is allowed to advertise on Google.
Review where competitors send paid traffic and what their websites look like.
Look for pages that fail to explain how the business helps, how to contact it, and whether it has proof such as testimonials or case studies.
Use competitor weaknesses to find a practical advantage.

quote.text: The first thing to look at is can I even advertise like am I even allowed to advertise that on Google?
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Make the landing page answer three questions quickly
steps: State how the business helps the visitor.
Show reviews or testimonials as proof.
Make contact or booking easy to find.
Put those answers where a visitor can see them in the first three to five seconds.

quote.text: If your website can answer those three things in the first 3 to 5 seconds, you have a good website.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Structure a YouTube lead generation ad to earn the click
steps: Use an in-stream ad.
Use the first five seconds to call out the intended customer and filter out others.
Describe the customer's problem, explain how the offer helps, and ask for the click.
Let the landing page generate the lead and the sales conversation generate the sale.

quote.text: Your ad generates a click. Your landing page generates the lead. And then when they talk to you, you generate the sale.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Use clear audio and a relevant script for YouTube placements
steps: Write a script that calls out the intended audience and problem.
Use a good phone and a microphone rather than assuming expensive equipment is required.
Check that audio and video quality are adequate so the campaign does not land in poor placements.

quote.text: You just need this like a good h a good phone, you know, with a nice DJI mic or whatever.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Build layered YouTube and remarketing campaigns
steps: Start with Google Ads and establish a regular flow of leads and an acceptable acquisition cost.
Add YouTube lead generation targeting in-market audiences, relevant search terms, and competitor websites.
Add broad brand awareness in the chosen service radius when lead generation is working.
Track website visitors and run remarketing through YouTube, display, and Facebook.
Use a special offer for remarketing visitors who did not convert.

quote.text: Once I got Google ads up and running and it's I'm getting regular leads, I know my target se I know what my target cost per acquisition is
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Improve campaigns with small regular tests
steps: Test one part of the top of the landing page, such as the headline.
Review ad copy and click-through rate.
Make small changes regularly and compare results.

quote.text: Just all these little bits once a month makes a huge huge difference.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Create a lead follow-up sequence
steps: Measure call show rate rather than judging campaigns only by lead volume.
Use more than a single email reminder for booked calls.
Consider reminder messages, while ensuring that contact is permitted and compliant.

quote.text: what's your follow-up sequence do you have emails going out reminder emails going out do you have text messages
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Get testimonials before scaling a new business
steps: Reach out to people in your network and explain the service.
Offer to do initial work for free in exchange for a testimonial.
Use the testimonials on the landing page as proof.
Ask satisfied clients for introductions to relevant contacts.

quote.text: I will help you with this. All I want is a testimonial. You have to pay me nothing. All I want is a testimonial.
quote.speaker: Marcus

tactics.name: Give campaigns time to mature
steps: Do not stop a campaign after a small number of disappointing calls.
Review the landing page, follow-up, show rate, and closing process before deciding that ads do not work.
Allow at least the stated three-month period for the system to get established.

quote.text: So, you need to be patient. This is like a threemonth process minimum to really get this humming.
quote.speaker: Marcus
